title: File permissions
body:
ls -l shows permissions like -rw-r--r--: owner, group, others, each with read, write, execute. Mode 600 means only the owner can read and write; 644 lets everyone read.

Permissions protect one file, not its copies. A readable backup of a private file leaks it.

Defenders: least privilege, and give backups the same protection as the original.

How to spot it: run ls -l and look for a final r in the third group (others can read) on files that should be private, and for backup or copy files with looser modes than the original.
